key_insight: Localizing repeated phase-field fracture solves to an adaptive crack-tip patch preserves reference accuracy while substantially reducing computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes large-scale brittle-fracture simulations more practical by concentrating resolution and solution effort near advancing cracks.
method: Adaptively refine and coarsen the mesh around active crack-tip patches.
Condense the inactive exterior onto the patch interface using a Schur complement, reusing its factorization while the patch stays fixed.
Freeze the exterior phase field and implement the localized formulation in FEniCSx.
evidence_signal: Across quasi-static, dynamic branching, 3D mixed-mode, and crack-coalescence tests, global quantities differed from reference solutions by less than 0.5%; surfing-test speedups rose from 6.9× to 22.8× when domain size doubled.
watch_item: Freezing the exterior phase field introduces a crack-wake approximation; patch updates must capture evolving fracture activity.
paper_title: Adaptive Crack-Tip Localization of Phase-Field Fracture Computations
